test_frozendict_signature.py.rationale: Change A registers frozendict in the builtins signature registry with dict-like call shapes. These tests check that the entry exists and gives dict semantics: no arguments, a single mapping, or keywords are valid, and two positional arguments are not. They also drive a signature-less callable through the public introspection helpers and curry, so the registry spec is checked on any Python version, not only 3.15.

test_compose_annotations.py.rationale: Change B exposes combined __annotations__ on Compose, built the same way as __signature__. These tests check the combined view when builtins and curried functions sit at either end of the composition. Those callables are introspected through the signature registry that change A extends, and the annotations must stay consistent with inspect.signature and typing.get_type_hints.

test_introspection_invariants.py.rationale: Both changes touch the introspection machinery. A extends the builtin signature registry, and B adds class-level attributes and an optional annotationlib import to toolz.functoolz. Every public callable in toolz.functoolz must stay introspectable, and the registry-based introspection of Compose and composed callables must keep working on every tree.
